raw_response:
The plot displays the accuracy (ACC %) of five different methods — Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME — as a function of the co-occurrence number, which is plotted on a logarithmic x-axis ranging from 1 to 1000. The y-axis represents accuracy in percentage, ranging from 40% to 65%. Each method is represented by a distinct colored line with a unique marker: Base (black solid line with circle markers), MEND (brown dashed line with diamond markers), FT (blue dashed line with triangle markers), MEMIT (purple dashed line with star markers), and ROME (green solid line with square markers). The Base method starts at approximately 39% accuracy at a co-occurrence number of 1 and increases slightly to about 44% at 1000. The MEND method begins at around 44% and rises to about 57%. The FT method starts at 40% and increases to approximately 47%. The MEMIT method begins at about 44% and rises to around 55%. The ROME method starts at approximately 51% and increases steadily to about 66%. All lines show a general upward trend as the co-occurrence number increases, with ROME consistently achieving the highest accuracy and Base the lowest. The plot features a grid background for easier reading of data points.
